nodes.name: NF-PBA Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.119 g of Na₄Fe(CN)₆·10H₂O (Aladdin, analytical reagent) was added in 250 mL of water to obtain solution A. Then, 5.882 g of Na₃C₆H₅O₇ (Aladdin, analytical reagent) and 1 g of NiCl₂·6H₂O (Aladdin, analytical reagent) were added to another 250 mL of water to obtain solution B. Then, solution A was poured into solution B, and the mixture was aged at room temperature for 48 h to get the precipitate. After that, the as-obtained NaₓNiFe(CN)₆ nanocubes were filtered, washed with deionized water, and dried overnight in vacuum oven at 100°C.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH with activation process
nodes.source_text: Chronopotentiometric measurements at a constant current density of 20 mA cm^{-2} indicated an activation process... the NF-PBA-A sample has an impressively low overpotential of only 258 mV to reach a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2}. The current density on NF-PBA-A at an overpotential of 304 mV can reach 61 mA cm^{-2}... The decreased Tafel slope of 46 mV dec^{-1}... The activated NF-PBA-A exhibited much lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct) than pristine NF-PBA.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of NF-PBA shows diffraction peaks agreeing with previous NiFe PBA structures confirming cubic crystal structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) characterized the crystal structure of the as-prepared catalyst. The diffraction peaks of NF-PBA in Figure 1a agreed well with previous NiFe PBA structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows NF-PBA has cubic morphology with dimensions of about 200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image in Figure 1b showed that the catalyst has a cubic morphology with dimensions of about 200 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms cubic structure of NF-PBA with FFT analysis showing (020), (200), and (220) faces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This was confirmed with transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure 1c). The inset of Figure 1c showed fast Fourier transform (FFT) analysis of the high-resolution TEM image, including (020), (200), and (220) faces.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping reveals homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, and C elements throughout NF-PBA structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping revealed homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, and C elements throughout the catalyst structures (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS of Ni in NF-PBA shows 6-fold coordination with Ni-N bond length of 2.08 Å; Fe shows Fe-C bond length of 1.90 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra of NF-PBA (Figures 1e and S1) identified a 6-fold coordination structure of Ni with the nearest Ni-N bond length of 2.08 Å; Fe was coordinated with six carbon atoms for an average Fe-C bond length of 1.90 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L-edge s-XAS shows Ni2+ high-spin configuration similar to NiO; Fe L-edge shows low-spin Fe2+ in NF-PBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni L-edge spectra had the same features as NiO, suggesting that the Ni2+ oxidation state has a high-spin configuration in NF-PBA (Figure S2). The Fe in NF-PBA was low-spin Fe2+ (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of NF-PBA-A shows transformation from initial cubic morphology to shapeless morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image (Figure S9) and the TEM image (Figure 3a) indicated that initial cubic morphology of NF-PBA transformed into shapeless morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS of NF-PBA-A shows distribution of Ni and O elements with almost no Fe and N signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping results exhibited a distribution of Ni and O elements of remaining catalyst, while almost no Fe and N signals were detected. This observation was further supported by the energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) data (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of NF-PBA-A shows amorphous nature with only peaks from carbon paper, no NF-PBA signal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amorphous nature of the NF-PBA-A was confirmed via the XRD pattern that exhibited only peaks from the carbon paper (Figures 3c and S10); no signal of NF-PBA was seen.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES of NF-PBA-A matches Ni(OH)2 reference, confirming analogous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) was performed on the Ni K-edge of NF-PBA-A as well as NiO and Ni(OH)2 references (Figure 3d). The XANES structures of NF-PBA-A were consistent with that of Ni(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ni K-edge XAS shows 1.7 eV edge shift at 1.50 V indicating Ni2+ oxidation to higher valence states, reversible and potential-dependent.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy position of the absorption edge gradually shifted to higher energy with increasing potential, i.e., the spectra showed a distinct edge shift of 1.7 eV under catalytic potential of 1.50 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando FT-EXAFS shows Ni-O bond length contraction from 2.04 Å (Ni2+) to 1.99 Å (Ni2+/3+) to 1.89 Å (Ni3+/4+) with constant coordination number.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the initial NF-PBA-A structure, the average Ni-O bond length was 2.04 Å... When a low potential was applied, the Ni-O bond length decreased to 1.99 Å... Further oxidation to Ni3+/Ni4+ was confirmed by the shrinking of Ni-O bond length to 1.89 Å.
